## Writer identification with a CNN

<!-- Task 2: build and evaluate a CNN with writer ID as the response; overall and per-digit performance; what the measures mean in real-world terms. -->

The prediction task is closed-set writer identification: given a single 28 x 28 image of a digit, the model predicts which of the 20 writers produced it. The CNN follows the structure of the lecture example (@tbl-cnn-structure). It was trained on sessions 1-3, with session 4 used for validation and to decide when to stop training. Session 5 was held out as the test set, ensuring that all test images come from a session not seen during training.

```{r}
#| label: cnn-cache

# After changing any of the training code, delete the file and render again.
cnn_results_file <- "results/cnn_split.rds"
cnn_retrain <- !file.exists(cnn_results_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: cnn-split
#| eval: !expr cnn_retrain

# Split by session: sessions 1-3 train, session 4 validation, session 5 test
train_id <- which(handwriting$metadata$session <= 3)
val_id <- which(handwriting$metadata$session == 4)
test_id <- which(handwriting$metadata$session == 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: cnn-preprocess
#| eval: !expr cnn_retrain

# Scale pixel values to 0,1
x <- handwriting$images / 255
x_train <- x[train_id,,,,drop = FALSE]
x_val <- x[val_id,,,,drop = FALSE]
x_test <- x[test_id,,,,drop = FALSE]

y <- to_categorical(handwriting$metadata$person_id - 1, 20)
y_train <- y[train_id,]
y_val <- y[val_id,]
y_test <- y[test_id,]
```

```{r}
#| label: cnn-define
#| eval: !expr cnn_retrain

set_random_seed(67)

input <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))

# from lecture slides
output <- input %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 16, kernel_size = c(3,3)) %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.20) %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 16, kernel_size = c(3,3), activation = "relu") %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2)) %>%
  layer_flatten() %>%
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = 'softmax')

model <- keras_model(inputs = input, outputs = output)
cnn_summary <- capture.output(print(model))

model %>% compile(
  loss = 'categorical_crossentropy',
  optimizer = optimizer_adam(learning_rate = 0.01),
  metrics = c('accuracy'),
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cnn-fit
#| eval: !expr cnn_retrain

# Stop when accuracy on the validation session has not improved for 10 epochs,
# and go back to the weights from the best epoch
history <- model %>% fit(
  x_train, y_train,
  epochs = 100, batch_size = 8192,
  validation_data = list(x_val, y_val), shuffle = TRUE,
  verbose = 0,
  callbacks = list(
    callback_early_stopping(monitor = "val_accuracy", patience = 10,
                            restore_best_weights = TRUE)
  )
)

# Predictions for the validation and test sessions (op_argmax counts from 1, so this is the person_id)
y_val_hat <- model %>% predict(x_val, verbose = 0) %>% op_argmax(axis = 2) %>% as.numeric()
y_test_hat <- model %>% predict(x_test, verbose = 0) %>% op_argmax(axis = 2) %>% as.numeric()

# Save everything the rest of this section needs
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(summary = cnn_summary,
             history = tibble(epoch = seq_along(history$metrics$accuracy),
                              train = history$metrics$accuracy,
                              validation = history$metrics$val_accuracy),
             predictions = bind_rows(
               as_tibble(handwriting$metadata[val_id,]) %>% mutate(set = "validation", predicted = y_val_hat),
               as_tibble(handwriting$metadata[test_id,]) %>% mutate(set = "test", predicted = y_test_hat))),
        cnn_results_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: cnn-load

cnn_results <- readRDS(cnn_results_file)
cnn_test <- cnn_results$predictions %>% filter(set == "test")

# Numbers quoted in the text
cnn_pct <- function(x) paste0(format(round(100 * x, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
cnn_best_epoch <- cnn_results$history %>% slice_max(validation, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
cnn_plateau_epoch <- min(cnn_results$history$epoch[cnn_results$history$validation >= cnn_best_epoch$validation - 0.02])
cnn_test_accuracy <- mean(cnn_test$person_id == cnn_test$predicted)
cnn_digit <- cnn_test %>% group_by(digit) %>% summarise(accuracy = mean(person_id == predicted)) %>% arrange(desc(accuracy))
cnn_writer <- cnn_test %>% group_by(person_id) %>% summarise(accuracy = mean(person_id == predicted))
cnn_worst_confusion <- cnn_test %>% filter(person_id != predicted) %>% count(person_id, predicted, sort = TRUE) %>% slice(1)
```

### Model structure

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cnn-structure
#| tbl-cap: "Layers of the CNN used for writer identification, with the shape of each layer's output and its number of trainable parameters."

# The saved Keras summary is text: keep the rows of its table and split them into columns
cnn_layers <- cnn_results$summary %>%
  str_subset("^│") %>%
  str_split_fixed("│", 5)

tibble(layer = str_trim(cnn_layers[, 2]),
       output_shape = str_trim(cnn_layers[, 3]),
       parameters = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(str_remove_all(cnn_layers[, 4], "[, ]")))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(parameters)) %>% # drops the header row of the Keras summary
  add_row(layer = "Total", output_shape = "", parameters = sum(.$parameters)) %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Layer (type)", "Output shape", "Parameters"),
               align = "llr")
```

### Training

```{r}
#| label: fig-cnn-history
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy of the CNN after each epoch on the training sessions (1-3) and the validation session (4). Training stopped once validation accuracy had not improved for 10 epochs."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5

cnn_results$history %>%
  pivot_longer(c(train, validation), names_to = "data", values_to = "accuracy") %>%
  mutate(data = recode(data, train = "Training (sessions 1-3)", validation = "Validation (session 4)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = epoch, y = accuracy, colour = data)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Epoch", y = "Accuracy", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Writer identification performance

#### What the evaluation measures capture

In real-world terms, accuracy represents the proportion of handwritten digit images correctly attributed to the writer, assuming the writer is one of the 20 enrolled individuals and the digit was written in a session not used for training. A system based on this model would correctly identify the writer from a single digit approximately half the time. However, this measure says nothing about individuals outside the 20 enrolled writers, as the model would still assign images to one of them. Accuracy by digit indicates which digits may contain more writer-specific information, while the confusion matrix shows which writers are most frequently mistaken for one another. This is particularly relevant when an incorrect attribution has consequences for the person identified.

#### Results of the basic CNN

On the test session, the CNN named the correct writer for `r cnn_pct(cnn_test_accuracy)` of images (@tbl-cnn-accuracy), compared with 5% expected baseline (random guessing). Accuracy differed by digit (@tbl-cnn-by-digit): it was highest for digit `r cnn_digit$digit[1]` (`r cnn_pct(cnn_digit$accuracy[1])`) and lowest for digit `r cnn_digit$digit[5]` (`r cnn_pct(cnn_digit$accuracy[5])`). Each digit has 1000 test images from the single session that was not used in training or validation.

#### Error analysis

Errors were concentrated in particular writers (@tbl-cnn-confusion). `r str_to_sentence(xfun::numbers_to_words(sum(cnn_writer$accuracy >= 0.95)))` writers were identified in at least 95% of their images, whereas writers `r knitr::combine_words(cnn_writer$person_id[cnn_writer$accuracy <= 0.05])` were identified in at most 5% of theirs; for example, `r cnn_worst_confusion$n` of the 250 images from writer `r cnn_worst_confusion$person_id` were attributed to writer `r cnn_worst_confusion$predicted`.

#### Overfitting

The CNN overfits to the training sessions (@fig-cnn-history). Validation accuracy came within two percentage points of its maximum (`r cnn_pct(cnn_best_epoch$validation)`) by epoch `r cnn_plateau_epoch` and then stayed flat, while training accuracy kept rising to `r cnn_pct(max(cnn_results$history$train))` by the end of training at epoch `r nrow(cnn_results$history)`. The later epochs therefore appear to have fitted features of the training sessions that did not generalise to a new session. Validation accuracy did not fall, so the additional training gave no benefit. For this reason, the hyperparameter search uses the earliest epoch whose validation accuracy was within one standard error of the best observed value, rather than continuing training unnecessarily.


```{r}
#| label: tbl-cnn-accuracy
#| tbl-cap: "Overall writer identification accuracy of the CNN on the validation session (used for early stopping) and on the untouched test session."

cnn_results$predictions %>%
  mutate(set = factor(set, levels = c("validation", "test"),
                      labels = c("Validation (session 4)", "Test (session 5)"))) %>%
  group_by(set) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), accuracy = 100 * mean(person_id == predicted)) %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Set", "Images", "Accuracy (%)"),
               digits = 1, align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cnn-by-digit
#| tbl-cap: "Writer identification accuracy of the CNN on the test session for each digit, from most to least accurate."

cnn_test %>%
  group_by(digit) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), accuracy = 100 * mean(person_id == predicted)) %>%
  arrange(desc(accuracy)) %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Digit", "Images", "Accuracy (%)"),
               digits = 1, align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cnn-confusion
#| tbl-cap: "Confusion matrix of the CNN on the test session. Each row is the true writer (250 test images each) and each column the writer the CNN predicted, so reading across a row shows where that writer's images went. Green: at least half of a writer's images correctly identified. Red: at least a third of a writer's images attributed to the same wrong writer."

y_test_original <- factor(cnn_test$person_id, levels = 1:20)
y_test_hat <- factor(cnn_test$predicted, levels = 1:20)

cnn_confusion <- table(y_test_original, y_test_hat) %>% as.data.frame.matrix()
cnn_writer_n <- rowSums(cnn_confusion)

# Colour each count by the share of the true writer's images it holds: green on the diagonal
# (correct) from one half, red off the diagonal (one wrong writer) from one third
cnn_confusion_coloured <- map2_dfc(cnn_confusion, seq_along(cnn_confusion), function(counts, j) {
  share <- counts / cnn_writer_n
  colour <- case_when(seq_along(counts) == j & share >= 0.5 ~ "#008300",
                      seq_along(counts) != j & share >= 1/3 ~ "#d03b3b")
  cells <- as.character(counts)
  coloured <- !is.na(colour)
  cells[coloured] <- cell_spec(counts[coloured], format = "html", color = colour[coloured], bold = TRUE)
  cells
})

cnn_confusion_coloured %>%
  mutate(true_writer = rownames(cnn_confusion), .before = 1) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = "r", col.names = c("True writer", names(cnn_confusion))) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Predicted writer" = ncol(cnn_confusion))) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```
